comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Change 1688 pushed for review (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1688), commit 7e18818638, stacked on 1687.

Implemented as planned, three files:
- .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml: job-level permissions block adding id-token: write (and RESTATING contents: write + actions: write -- a job-level block replaces the workflow-level one wholesale, so omitting either would have silently broken commit-back / re-dispatch). OIDC step mirrors the Bedrock CI arm in structured-output-baseline.yml (aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6, role + region from repo vars), gated on always() + canonical repo + var-set so forks and unconfigured checkouts skip it. Then put-metric-data 1 on failure() / 0 on success().
- infra/terraform/iam_bridge_metrics.tf: NEW role rebar-bridge-metrics. No existing role widened.
- infra/terraform/monitoring_bridge.tf: alarm rebar-bridge-run-failures.

Two design points worth the record:
1. Publishing 0 on success rather than relying on missing-data semantics. With treat_missing_data=notBreaching a failure-only metric alarms correctly, but it is ABSENT whenever healthy -- indistinguishable from 'the publisher is broken or lost PutMetricData', and the alarm sits in INSUFFICIENT_DATA rather than OK. The steady 0 makes the publisher itself observable, matching how observability.sh publishes gerrit_healthy/reviewbot_healthy every tick.
2. Cadence deviates from the rebar-autodeploy-* 900s/threshold-0 style, deliberately: period 3600 / threshold 1 / GreaterThanThreshold, so the SECOND failure in an hour pages (~40 min detection). The bridge runs every ~20 min and a lone failed pass is usually a transient blip, while the failure worth paging for (expired token) fails every pass. Total absence of runs stays owned by the Reconciler Heartbeat Canary -- notBreaching means this alarm cannot see it, and that is noted in the description.

The metric steps are placed LAST in the job so failure() also covers a failed re-dispatch, and are continue-on-error so telemetry can never turn a converged reconcile pass red.

Local gates: actionlint clean; terraform fmt -check + validate pass; alarm_description is 896 chars (under the 1024 cap validate enforces); 88 workflow-related unit tests pass; make lint clean. zizmor reports unpinned-uses on my @v6 pin, but it does so for every action already in this file (checkout@v7, setup-python@v7, cache@v6) and CI scopes zizmor to release.yml only -- pinning mine alone would be inconsistent with the file.

OPERATOR ACTION after apply: set repo Variables AWS_BRIDGE_METRICS_ROLE_ARN (terraform output bridge_metrics_role_arn) and AWS_BRIDGE_METRICS_REGION. Until both are set the workflow skips the metric steps entirely and behaves exactly as before -- so merge is safe ahead of the apply.

APPLY AUTHORIZATION + PROVENANCE (recorded so the chain is tracker-visible rather than living only in agent context).

The terraform apply for this ticket is pre-authorized. The authorization did NOT originate in the store: the operator approved it in response to the apply-pending framing, and it reached me via a coordinator relay of that approval. This comment's own timestamp is the authoritative date of the relay; the underlying alarm sweep it came from is the 2026-08-12 AWS investigation recorded on childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet (b902-18af-14ed-4da1) comment 12.

Recording this because the earlier lorikeet record lists both follow-ups as 'surfaced for operator decision' with no written approval in the store -- so without this note the apply would look self-authorized on a later read.

DIVISION OF LABOUR, as relayed: the COORDINATOR runs the apply after change 1688 merges, inspecting the plan first. I do not touch AWS. When the coordinator confirms the apply, I tick AC5 and close this ticket fully; until that confirmation arrives the ticket stays in_progress.

EXPECTED PLAN for the coordinator to verify against -- 3 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy:
  + aws_iam_role.gha_bridge_metrics              (rebar-bridge-metrics)
  + aws_iam_role_policy.gha_bridge_metrics_put   (rebar-bridge-metrics-put; cloudwatch:PutMetricData conditioned on cloudwatch:namespace = rebar/host)
  + aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.bridge_run_failures  (rebar-bridge-run-failures)
  plus a new output, bridge_metrics_role_arn.

Anything beyond those three adds -- in particular ANY diff against aws_iam_role.gha_terraform_plan, its attached policies, or the Bedrock role -- means this change widened an existing role and the plan should be rejected rather than applied.

POST-APPLY, before AC5 can be ticked: set repo Variables AWS_BRIDGE_METRICS_ROLE_ARN (= terraform output bridge_metrics_role_arn) and AWS_BRIDGE_METRICS_REGION. The workflow skips its metric steps while either is unset, so the metric only begins flowing once both exist. Proof for AC5: aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --alarm-names rebar-bridge-run-failures returns the alarm.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The Jira API-token outage took the Reconcile Bridge down and produced **zero CloudWatch
signal**. The bridge runs on GitHub Actions, not on the monitored host, so nothing in
`infra/scripts/observability.sh` (the host probe that publishes every `rebar/host` metric) can
see it. Its only failure surface today is `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:264-279`
("Notify on bridge failure"), which writes a step summary and an `::error` annotation — visible
only to someone already looking at the run. GitHub Actions *can* publish to CloudWatch; nothing
in this repo does it yet.

## Design

**(a) Publish the metric from the workflow.** Add to the `reconcile` job in
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`:

- `id-token: write` at **job** level (the workflow-level block at :58-60 is `contents: write` +
  `actions: write`; job-level is where `structured-output-baseline.yml:39-41` puts it for the
  same reason).
- an OIDC credential step mirroring `structured-output-baseline.yml:60-67`
  (`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6`, `role-to-assume` + `aws-region` from repo
  `vars`), gated on `always()` so it is present on both the success and failure paths, and on
  the canonical repo + the var being set so forks and unconfigured checkouts skip it.
- `bridge_run_failures = 1` on `if: failure()`, and `= 0` on `if: success()`, both
  `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --namespace rebar/host --metric-name bridge_run_failures
  --unit Count --value <n>`, dimensionless on both sides (`monitoring_s4b.tf`: a dimension on
  only one side silently unmatches the alarm).

*Why publish 0 on success rather than relying on missing-data semantics:* with
`treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"` a failure-only metric would alarm correctly, but the
metric would be absent whenever things are healthy — indistinguishable from "the publisher
itself is broken/unauthorized", and the alarm would sit in `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` rather than `OK`.
The success-path 0 makes the *publisher* continuously observable, matching the existing host
probe, which publishes `gerrit_healthy`/`reviewbot_healthy` as 0-or-1 every tick rather than
only on failure (`observability.sh:45-51`). Telemetry steps are `continue-on-error` so a
metric publish can never fail an otherwise-converged reconcile pass.

**(b) IAM.** Do **not** widen `rebar-terraform-plan` (`iam.tf:144-199`, `ReadOnlyAccess` +
`kms:Decrypt` — it is the drift-detection role and single-owner) and do not widen the Bedrock CI
role. Add a **new** narrowly-scoped role in `infra/terraform`, reusing the repo's existing OIDC
pattern: trust `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github` (`oidc.tf:14`) with the same
`aud = sts.amazonaws.com` + `sub` StringLike `repo:navapbc/rebar:*` conditions, and one inline
policy granting **only** `cloudwatch:PutMetricData`, constrained by the standard
`cloudwatch:namespace` StringEquals condition to `rebar/host`. PutMetricData takes no resource
ARN, so the namespace condition is what makes it narrow.

**(c) Alarm.** A new CloudWatch alarm on `rebar/host:bridge_run_failures`, styled on the
`rebar-autodeploy-*` alarms (`monitoring_autodeploy.tf:113-150`): `Sum`, dimensionless,
`treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"`, SNS `alarm_actions` + `ok_actions`, description naming
the runbook action (open the workflow run; check Jira token validity). Cadence differs
deliberately from the autodeploy 900s/threshold-0: the bridge runs every ~20 min, so a single
failed pass is routinely a transient network/API blip, while the token outage was sustained.
`period = 3600` with `threshold = 1` / `GreaterThanThreshold` alarms on the **second** failed
pass within an hour — a flake stays quiet, a real outage pages within ~40 minutes.

## Testing

- `actionlint .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` and `zizmor .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`
  (workflow edits are gated on both in CI).
- `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` in `infra/terraform` (validate previously caught
  an over-cap `alarm_description`; the 1024-char limit applies).
- `pytest tests/scripts -q` for the unchanged script suites (no regression from the workflow edit).
- The apply itself is operator-run; post-apply proof is
  `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --alarm-names rebar-bridge-run-failures` returning the alarm.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `reconcile-bridge.yml` publishes `rebar/host:bridge_run_failures` = 1 on `if: failure()` and
      0 on `if: success()`, authenticated by OIDC via repo `vars`, skipped outside the canonical
      repo, and `continue-on-error` so telemetry cannot fail a converged pass. Checked:
      `actionlint` + `zizmor` clean on the edited workflow.
- [ ] A new IAM role in `infra/terraform` grants exactly `cloudwatch:PutMetricData` conditioned on
      `cloudwatch:namespace = rebar/host`, federating the existing
      `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github`. Checked: no diff widens `rebar-terraform-plan` or
      the Bedrock CI role (`git diff` touches neither).
- [ ] An `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` on the new metric exists, dimensionless, with
      `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"`, SNS `alarm_actions` + `ok_actions`, and a description
      naming the runbook action (open the workflow run; check Jira token validity). Checked:
      `terraform fmt -check` + `terraform validate` pass.
- [ ] Change lands on `main` through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
- [ ] The operator has run `terraform apply` for the new role + alarm and the alarm exists in
      CloudWatch. **This AC is the operator's apply; the implementing agent cannot satisfy it.**
      Checked: `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --alarm-names rebar-bridge-run-failures`.
